chunks: The Imamate is a covenant from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, covenanted to specifically named men. It is not for the Imam to withhold it from the one who comes after him. Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed to Dawud (peace be upon him): 'Take a successor from your family, for it has preceded in My knowledge that I will not send a prophet except that he shall have a successor from his family.' Dawud (peace be upon him) had several children, and among them was a boy whose mother was with Dawud, and he loved her.

So Dawud (peace be upon him) went to her when the revelation came to him and said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has revealed to me, commanding me to take a successor from my family.' His wife said to him: 'Let it be my son.' He said: 'That is what I intend.' And what had preceded in the inevitable knowledge of Allah was that it would be Sulayman. So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed to Dawud: 'Do not be hasty before My command comes to you.' It was not long before two men who were disputing about sheep and a vineyard came to Dawud (peace be upon him). So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Dawud: 'Gather your sons; whoever judges this case correctly shall be your successor after you.'

So Dawud (peace be upon him) gathered his children. When the two disputants presented their case, Sulayman (peace be upon him) said: 'O owner of the vineyard, when did this man's sheep enter your vineyard?' He said: 'They entered it at night.' He said: 'I rule against you, O owner of the sheep, with the offspring of your sheep and their wool for this year of yours.' Then Dawud said to him: 'Why did you not rule by taking the sheep themselves, when the scholars of the Children of Israel assessed it so, and the price of the vineyard was equal to the value of the sheep?' Sulayman said: 'The vineyard was not uprooted from its root — only its fruit was eaten, and it will return next year.'

Then God Almighty revealed to Dawud: 'Verily the ruling in this case is what Sulayman ruled. O Dawud, you intended one thing and We intended another.' So Dawud went to his wife and said: 'We intended a thing, and God Almighty intended something else, and nothing prevailed but what God Almighty willed. So we are pleased with the command of God Almighty and submit to it.' And likewise the successors (peace be upon them) — it is not for them to overstep in this matter and pass it to someone other than its rightful holder.

Al-Kulayni said: The meaning of the first hadith is that if the sheep had entered the vineyard during the day, nothing would be owed by the owner of the sheep — because the owner of the sheep has the right to let his sheep graze during the day, while it is the responsibility of the vineyard owner to guard it. And upon the owner of the sheep is the obligation to tether his sheep at night, while the vineyard owner has the right to sleep in his house.

key_terms.الأوصياء: The successors — the chain of Imams, each designated by the previous one under divine command
key_terms.الإمامة: Imamate — the divinely appointed leadership role after the Prophet
key_terms.عهد: Covenant — a binding divine designation, not a human appointment
key_terms.مُسَمَّيْنَ: Specifically named — Imams are named by God, not elected or chosen by community consensus
key_terms.وصي: Successor/legatee — the divinely designated inheritor of prophetic and Imamic authority

ai.seo_question: What does al-Kafi teach about the nature of the Imamate as a divine covenant?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that the Imamate is a divine covenant from Allah designating specific, named individuals — it cannot be withheld or transferred by the Imam's personal will. Using the story of the Prophet Dawud and his son Sulayman as a Quranic precedent, the hadith demonstrates that divine succession is predetermined in God's eternal knowledge and cannot be altered by human preference, even that of a beloved spouse. The narrative concludes with al-Kulayni's explanatory note on the subsidiary legal ruling about sheep grazing liability, contextualizing the test that revealed Sulayman's fitness for succession.
